key_insight: ERUnderstand is the first large-scale benchmark designed to test whether vision-language models can truly understand structured Entity-Relationship diagrams, not just recognize their visual appearance. It fills a major gap by turning ERD understanding into a measurable AI evaluation task.
problem_solved: AI systems struggle to use ER diagrams because they are usually stored as images rather than machine-readable schemas, making database design and analysis hard to automate. This paper addresses the lack of a standard benchmark for evaluating structured ER diagram understanding.
method: Introduces ERUnderstand, a benchmark of 2,960 ER diagrams.
Covers diverse sources including educational materials, real-world schemas, and synthetic examples.
Includes variation in domain, notation, and diagram complexity to evaluate robustness across settings.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers and practitioners a standardized way to measure how well vision-language models can interpret database design diagrams. It can accelerate progress toward AI tools for schema extraction, database engineering, and diagram-based reasoning.
visual_elements: Benchmark overview pipeline showing diagram sources, normalization, and evaluation
Bar chart comparing model performance across diagram types and complexity levels
Example ER diagram with highlighted entities, relationships, and attributes
Icon set representing educational, real-world, and synthetic data sources
paper_title: ERUnderstand: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Structured ER Diagrams
paper_authors: Ali Ansari, Yasmin Mohammadi, Farnoush Nili, Parsa Esmaeilkhani, Longin Jan Latecki
